findings.stemStart: Which service adjustment can rescue a red that
findings.problem: The keyed answer told the student to serve a too-tannic red cooler, which is backwards: cold hardens tannin, as this module's own red-too-cold question and the original explanation both state. The accept list graded 'chill it' and 'lower the temperature'.
findings.fix: ans 'Decant it, or serve it a touch warmer'; accept drops every cooler, chill and lower-temperature entry and takes decant, aerate and warmer phrasings; exp rewritten to say that air softens tannin and a too-cool red gains from a few degrees.
findings.source: Tannin and bitterness are perceived more strongly at low temperature (standard service teaching); the module's own question 'Serving a red too cold does what to its tannin and bitterness?' keys 'Increases both'.

findings.stemStart: A dish's sweetness sets a floor for the
findings.problem: The stem's word 'floor' gives away the key ('at least as sweet'), and the distractor 'Sweetness in food has no bearing' contradicts the stem's own premise, so the question could be answered from its wording.
findings.fix: Two distractors replaced with floor-shaped misconceptions ('The wine's acidity must at least match the dish's sugar', 'The wine needs alcohol enough to stand up to the sugar'); key lengthened to 'The wine must be at least as sweet as the dish itself' so the four sit within 3 characters; exp extended to cover acidity and alcohol.
findings.source: standard pairing teaching (WSET and CMS food and wine principles); README rule that a stem must not be answerable from its own words

findings.stemStart: Asparagus is difficult with wine because of which
findings.problem: The explanation contradicted itself: it said the pyrazines in asparagus and Sauvignon Blanc compound each other, then called Sauvignon the escape.
findings.fix: exp rewritten: asparagus carries the same green pyrazines that mark Sauvignon, that vegetal edge thins most wines, and Sauvignon escapes by echoing the greenness.
findings.source: standard pairing teaching (WSET and CMS food and wine principles) (Sauvignon Blanc with asparagus is the textbook complement)

findings.stemStart: Why is white wine often a better partner
findings.problem: Two distractors were not real misconceptions ('Red wine is always served too cold for cheese', 'Cheese contains no fat to speak of'), leaving the key as the only plausible option.
findings.fix: Replaced with 'Salt in cheese strips a red of its fruit' and 'Whites carry more tannin to bind the protein', both false and plausible; exp adds that salt, if anything, flatters a red's fruit.
findings.source: standard pairing teaching (WSET and CMS food and wine principles) (salt lifts fruit and softens tannin; whites carry little tannin)

findings.stemStart: Melon with which style of sweet French fortified
findings.problem: Bare 'muscat' graded 'Muscat d'Alsace', a dry unfortified wine (the wrong-answer-contains-right class the README describes). Pineau des Charentes, the vin de liqueur traditionally poured with Charentais melon, was rejected.
findings.fix: Bare 'muscat' replaced with the fortified Muscats (de Rivesaltes, de Frontignan, de Lunel, de Mireval, fortified muscat, muscat vdn); 'pineau des charentes' added; exp names Pineau as a vin de liqueur playing the same part. Bare 'beaumes de venise' deliberately not added, since it would grade the dry red Rhone cru.
findings.source: lib.match_sa probe: 'muscat d alsace' graded before, rejected after; Pineau des Charentes is a vin de liqueur (grape must fortified with Cognac)

findings.stemStart: Which fortified wine is the traditional partner for
findings.problem: Banyuls and Maury, the classic French partners for dark chocolate, were marked wrong.
findings.fix: accept adds 'banyuls' and 'maury' (exact, under the existing ex=True); exp names them as the red vins doux naturels of Roussillon.
findings.source: standard pairing teaching (WSET and CMS food and wine principles); Banyuls with chocolate is a textbook pairing

findings.stemStart: Fat in a dish invites which two possible
findings.problem: The explanation said tannin 'binds the fat'; tannin binds protein, and its effect on fat is the sensory offset of astringency against a slick coating. The accept list also rejected 'acidity and tannin'.
findings.fix: exp now says tannin's drying grip offsets the coating fat leaves; accept adds the 'and' forms of acidity and tannin.
findings.source: Tannin-protein binding is the established mechanism (the module's own 'Tannin binding with protein' question); astringency and fattiness are opposing sensations

findings.stemStart: Which food element most reliably softens the perception
findings.problem: Under ex=True, 'protein', the primary mechanism and the module's own answer elsewhere, was marked wrong.
findings.fix: accept adds 'protein', 'proteins', 'proteins and fat' (exact).
findings.source: Tannin binding with protein (module's own question on rare beef)

findings.stemStart: A dish high in acidity demands what of
findings.problem: 'higher acidity', 'more acidity' and 'equal acidity' were all rejected.
findings.fix: accept adds those three. 'high acidity' was tried and dropped: cross_accept showed it would grade the Muscadet, Chablis and Champagne answer.

findings.stemStart: Salt in a dish does what to a
findings.problem: Natural two-part phrasings such as 'softens tannin and enhances fruit' were rejected.
findings.fix: accept adds five two-part phrasings, singular and plural.

findings.fix: accept adds 'more bitter', 'harder and more bitter', 'increases bitterness', 'accentuates bitterness'; probes confirm 'less bitter' still fails.

findings.fix: accept adds 'high acid', 'high acidity unoaked', 'unoaked high acidity', 'unoaked with high acidity'.

findings.fix: accept adds 'nutty', 'nuttiness', 'oxidised', 'amontillado'; 'not nutty' and 'fruity' still fail.

findings.stemStart: Goat cheese and Sauvignon Blanc succeed because both

findings.source: The question's own explanation; lib.match_sa probe

findings.fix: accept adds 'method', 'cooking technique', 'technique'.

findings.problem: Reversed orders such as 'alcohol and heat', and the spelling 'chili', were rejected.
findings.fix: accept adds six orders and spellings; 'alcohol and acidity' still fails.

findings.fix: accept adds four phrasings. Bare 'the guest' deliberately not added.

findings.fix: accept adds 'many dishes', 'many different dishes', 'wide range of dishes'.

findings.problem: 'serve it as ordered' and 'respect their choice' were rejected.
findings.fix: accept adds three phrasings; 'serve it without comment' was dropped after negation_probe flagged its 'without'.

findings.problem: The cause, 'the dessert is sweeter than the wine', the most natural answer to a why question, was rejected.
findings.fix: accept adds 'dessert is sweeter than the wine' and 'the wine is less sweet than the dessert'; the inversion 'the wine is sweeter than the dessert' still fails. 'not sweet enough' was dropped after negation_probe flagged it.

findings.problem: 'botrytised' alone and the spelling 'botrytized' were rejected.
findings.fix: accept adds 'botrytised', 'botrytized', 'botrytis wine'.

findings.stemStart: Warming a brandy balloon over a flame at
findings.problem: The keyed option read 'Poor practice, as heat coarsens the aroma', breaking the house rule against the word.
findings.fix: Key now 'A poor habit, as heat coarsens the aroma' (39 characters against 41, so the length spread is unchanged).
findings.source: House rule: never the word practice or practise

findings.fix: Now 'so lying them down does nothing for them'.

findings.stemStart: The label is turned toward one person at

findings.fix: Now 'Once the capsule is cut, a wrong bottle is the restaurant's loss', which states the intended point.
findings.source: Plain reading; standard presentation and service teaching

findings.stemStart: Ice alone chills a bottle slowly and unevenly.
findings.problem: 'dry ice cubes' reads as solid carbon dioxide.
findings.fix: Now 'ice on its own touches only a fraction of the glass'.

findings.stemStart: Every listed wine has a minimum quantity below
findings.problem: The stem defines the level below which a wine must be reordered, which many inventory systems call the reorder point; that answer was rejected.
findings.fix: accept adds 'reorder point', 'reorder level', 'minimum stock level'; exp notes that some systems call the trigger the reorder point.
findings.source: Hospitality inventory usage: par level and reorder point are used side by side, and par is often defined as the minimum on hand between deliveries

findings.fix: accept adds all three.

findings.fix: accept adds 'gentle hiss', 'soft hiss', 'quiet hiss'; 'a loud pop' still fails.

findings.fix: accept adds it (exact); bare 'port' and 'tawny port' still fail.

findings.stemStart: Merlot and Chardonnay with the grape named on
findings.problem: The explanation said Merlot and Cabernet reach the appellation map 'only' in Cabardes and Malepere. Limoux rouge is Merlot-led (45 to 70 per cent of the blend, Cabernet up to 35).
findings.fix: exp rewritten: the international varieties appear in appellations only where a decree makes room, with Chardonnay leading Limoux whites, Merlot leading Limoux reds and joining Cabernet in Cabardes and Malepere.
findings.source: Limoux interprofession (limoux-aoc.com, AOP Limoux rouge) and decree 2011-1788; WebSearch

findings.stemStart: Old bush-vine Carignan is not merely tolerated but
findings.problem: The appellation was renamed Boutenac (EU approval 14 March 2024), so the displayed answer named a superseded appellation. The explanation's blend figures for plantings, the 70 per cent group and the 80 per cent ceiling could not be confirmed (secondary sources disagree).
findings.fix: ans 'Boutenac, first named Corbieres-Boutenac' (accept already takes both names; bare 'Corbieres' still fails); exp keeps the confirmed 30 per cent Carignan floor and the four grapes, drops the unconfirmed figures, and records the 2024 rename.
findings.source: EU approval of the name change, March 2024 (trade reports and INAO 2020 Corbieres-Boutenac specification found by WebSearch)

findings.stemStart: A hilltop village of the Minervois earned in
findings.problem: The explanation named only Minervois-La-Liviniere, but the appellation has been La Liviniere since EU publication in March 2024 (and the old name was hyphenated wrongly).
findings.fix: exp now reads 'Minervois-La Liviniere' for 1999 and adds that since 2024 the appellation has carried the name La Liviniere alone; the keyed fact, the first village cru, is unchanged.
findings.source: EU Official Journal publication, March 2024, reported by trade and producer sources (WebSearch)

findings.stemStart: Pine woods ring a few dozen hectares of

findings.fix: exp now says the estate is the name most drinkers know the appellation by and keeps a long list of old permitted varieties.
findings.source: House rule: nothing volatile stated as fact

findings.fix: ans 'Fifty per cent' (already in the ex=True accept list, so it still grades).

verdicts.stemStart: Which service adjustment can rescue a red that
verdicts.why: The original key was wrong (cold hardens tannin) and the new key and explanation are right, but the containment list still graded the old backwards advice: match_sa took 'serve it slightly cooler, or decant it' and 'decant it and chill it' through the bare 'decant it' entry. Now ex=True with an exact list of decant, aerate and warmer phrasings and their two-part forms; probes confirm the cooler, chill and colder forms fail and the displayed answer grades.

verdicts.stemStart: A dish's sweetness sets a floor for the
verdicts.why: 'Sweetness in food has no bearing' did contradict the stem. The two new distractors are false, floor-shaped and close in length to the key, and the explanation's claim that sugar in food makes a strong dry wine taste hot matches standard teaching. The stem and id are unchanged.

verdicts.stemStart: Asparagus is difficult with wine because of which
verdicts.why: The old explanation did say the pyrazines compound each other and then called Sauvignon the escape. The new text is consistent with the stem and the module's complement teaching.

verdicts.stemStart: Why is white wine often a better partner
verdicts.why: Both old distractors were throwaways. The new ones are false and plausible, and the explanation's line on salt agrees with the module's own salt question (softens tannin, lifts fruit).

verdicts.stemStart: Melon with which style of sweet French fortified
verdicts.why: Bare 'muscat' did grade 'Muscat d'Alsace'. Refusing bare 'muscat' is defensible, since it names a grape rather than the style asked for. Pineau with Charentais melon is a real tradition, and the explanation calls it a vin de liqueur. One note: the finding says bare 'beaumes de venise' is not graded, but the 60 per cent containment branch grades it through 'muscat de beaumes de venise', as it did before the fix. That is harmless, because the stem already says sweet and fortified.

verdicts.stemStart: Which fortified wine is the traditional partner for
verdicts.why: Banyuls and Maury with dark chocolate is textbook, and the exact accept entries are right. But 'the red vins doux naturels of Roussillon' reads as the complete set, and Rivesaltes also makes red vins doux naturels (Grenat, Tuile). Now 'two red vins doux naturels of Roussillon'.

verdicts.stemStart: Fat in a dish invites which two possible
verdicts.why: Tannin binds protein, not fat, so the corrected mechanism is right. The 'and' forms name the same two responses. Probes reject the sweetness and alcohol pairs and 'neither acidity nor tannin'.

verdicts.stemStart: Which food element most reliably softens the perception
verdicts.why: The stem asks for a single element, so exact 'protein' should grade. Bare 'fat' still fails, which is a fair line.

verdicts.stemStart: A dish high in acidity demands what of
verdicts.why: Probes: 'higher', 'more' and 'equal acidity' grade; 'less acidity', 'lower acidity than the dish', 'no more acidity than the dish' and bare 'high acidity' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Salt in a dish does what to a
verdicts.why: Every addition restates the key. 'Hardens tannin and dulls fruit', 'more tannic and less fruity' and 'harder tannin and less fruit' still fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Umami in a dish, with no salt to
verdicts.why: The additions are restatements. 'Less bitter', 'reduces bitterness' and 'makes it softer, not more bitter' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Which two food tastes are broadly wine-friendly, tending
verdicts.why: Sour is the taste name for acid. 'Sweet and sour', 'sweet and salty' and 'bitter and sour' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Which two food tastes are broadly wine-hostile?
verdicts.why: A reversed order of an entry that already grades. 'Salt and acid' fails.

verdicts.stemStart: Serving a red too cold does what to
verdicts.why: The additions are restatements. 'Decreases both', 'less prominent', 'makes them softer' and 'reduces both' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Muscadet, Chablis and Champagne share which structural feature
verdicts.why: Exact restatements under ex=True. 'Oaked high acidity' and 'low acidity' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Hard aged cheeses such as Comte suit which
verdicts.why: Nutty is half the key, and amontillado sits beside the oloroso already listed. 'Non-oxidised' grades, because 'non' is not an engine negation word, but that is the same hole the original 'oxidative' entry already had ('non-oxidative' grades at HEAD). It is not new to this fix.

verdicts.stemStart: Goat cheese and Sauvignon Blanc succeed because both
verdicts.why: The additions are restatements. 'Sweetness and grassiness' and 'fat and grassiness' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Manchego alongside which fortified wine is a fixture
verdicts.why: The explanation itself names Fino and Amontillado, and every added style is a dry or naturally dry Sherry. Under ex=True, cream, pale cream, Port and Madeira fail.

verdicts.stemStart: The same chicken poached and then grilled calls
verdicts.why: 'Method' and 'technique' are the variable named in the key. The sauce, the protein, serving temperature, seasoning and the cut all fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Grilling and searing add which flavour dimension that
verdicts.why: Exact restatements of char and Maillard browning. Bare 'smoke', 'sweetness' and 'umami' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: A young tannic red with rare beef works
verdicts.why: Plural forms of the same mechanism. 'Tannin binds fat' and 'fat coats tannin' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Smoked foods sit badly with heavily oaked wine
verdicts.why: 'They amplify each other' and 'smoke on smoke' state the keyed reason. 'They clash' gives no reason at all, since it only restates the stem's 'sit badly', so it is removed. 'Smoke and oak clash', at HEAD, names the two elements and stays.

verdicts.stemStart: Poaching, steaming and raw preparations call for wines
verdicts.why: The additions are restatements. 'Full bodied', 'heavy wines' and 'oaked and full bodied' fail. 'Light bodied and heavily oaked' grades, which is a minor half-wrong case of the containment branch that the original list shared in kind.

verdicts.stemStart: Mint sauce with lamb is difficult for which
verdicts.why: The explanation calls it a vinegar problem. 'The fat', 'sugar' and 'sweetness' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Which treatment can turn a wine-hostile vegetable into
verdicts.why: Browning is in the key, and grilling browns as charring does. 'Steaming', 'boiling', 'boiling rather than grilling', 'pickling' and 'braising' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: A fiercely hot dish with a tannic, high-alcohol
verdicts.why: Reversed orders and the chili spelling. 'Alcohol and acidity', 'acidity and heat' and 'sweetness and heat' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: When a guest's stated preference conflicts with the
verdicts.why: Possessive forms of the key. 'The guest', 'the textbook pairing', 'the sommelier' and 'the host's preference' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Why is a by-the-glass programme built around food-friendly
verdicts.why: 'It cannot suit many dishes' grades, but in this stem it is a correct reason (a distinctive wine cannot), so it is no false positive. 'Few dishes' and 'they are cheaper' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: A guest orders a big Cabernet with sole.
verdicts.why: Restatements of serving as ordered. 'Suggest a white instead', 'refuse' and 'correct them' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Why does a dry sparkling wine struggle against
verdicts.why: The cause is a fair answer to a why question. Both inversions ('the wine is sweeter than the dessert', 'the dessert is less sweet than the wine') fail.

verdicts.stemStart: A fruit tart, as opposed to a chocolate
verdicts.why: Spelling and short forms of the key. 'Port', 'tawny port' and 'late harvest red' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Warming a brandy balloon over a flame at
verdicts.why: The house rule bans the word, and the new key keeps the meaning and the length spread.

verdicts.stemStart: Bottles are laid on their sides for a
verdicts.why: Removing the banned word was right, but 'lying them down' uses the intransitive verb transitively, and its 'them' pointed at the closures. Now 'so laying their bottles down does nothing for them'.

verdicts.stemStart: The label is turned toward one person at
verdicts.why: The old line read as false (an opened bottle is the guest's). The new line states the real point: a wrong bottle opened is the house's loss.

verdicts.stemStart: Ice alone chills a bottle slowly and unevenly.
verdicts.why: 'Dry ice' means solid carbon dioxide, so the fix is right.

verdicts.stemStart: Every listed wine has a minimum quantity below
verdicts.why: The stem's definition, the level that triggers a reorder, is exactly what inventory usage calls the reorder point, so accepting it is right. But 'minimum stock level' let the bare non-term 'stock level' grade through the 60 per cent containment branch. It is replaced by 'minimum stock', which still grades 'minimum stock level'. 'Stock level' and 'maximum stock' now fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Ginjo and daiginjo are separated from ordinary sake
verdicts.why: Seimai buai is a common romanisation. 'Alcohol content', 'smv' and 'sake meter value' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: A loud report and a plume of foam
verdicts.why: A soft hiss is the usual alternative description. 'A loud hiss', 'a loud pop', 'a pop' and 'a bang' fail.

verdicts.stemStart: Bottled unfiltered and throwing a heavy crust, which
verdicts.why: A single quinta vintage Port is a vintage Port. 'Port', 'tawny port', 'lbv' and 'late bottled vintage port' still fail under ex=True.

verdicts.stemStart: Merlot and Chardonnay with the grape named on
verdicts.why: Limoux rouge is Merlot-led, so the old 'only in Cabardes and Malepere' was wrong. The new sentence is accurate and claims no figures.

verdicts.why: The rename is confirmed: AOP Boutenac, OJEU 14 March 2024 (WebSearch). verdicts.stemStart: A hilltop village of the Minervois earned in
verdicts.why: The rename is confirmed: AOP La Liviniere, OJEU 26 March 2024 (WebSearch). 'Minervois-La Liviniere' is the official hyphenation, and the keyed fact is untouched.

verdicts.stemStart: Pine woods ring a few dozen hectares of
verdicts.why: A land share is volatile, and the module header bars ownership facts. The new line is safe and still true.
